To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the zirconosilicate framework structures can be divided into 41 topological classes, which are defined by 11 suprapolyhedaral invariants.
the MT frameworks of the zirconosilicate structures can be classified into 41 topological (structural) types.

the crystal structure of zirconosilosilicates is described by the MT(6) framework of topological type (2-2-2-3)(1-1-1-2), where T and M nodes form the PME with 4 and 2 connected tetrahedra, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the methodology of topological analysis of MT frameworks, which can be applied for the analysis of the structure of any MT compounds.
a comprehensive description of the MT-framework structures in zirconosilicate and their analogs.
the first step of classification and systematization of zirconosiles and their analogs based on the topological analysis of MT frameworks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the zirconosilicate structures are characterized by high structural complexity and variety, which can be explained by the presence of the same number of M and T atoms in the structure and by the high flexibility of the MT framework.
zirconosilicate and their analog structures represent the most complex topological type (41) of MT frameworks.
the structural diversity of zirconosilosilicates is determined by the complexity of their MT frameworks, which are formed by the combination of 12 PMEs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method of topological analysis of MT frameworks developed in this work is applicable for the classification of any complex MT structures.
the method of analysis and topological classification of mixed MT-frameworks is applicable to the structures of zirconates, silicates, germanates, and their solid solutions.
the method of topological analysis of MT frameworks and the concept of PME are useful tools for the study and classification of crystal structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the topological classification of crystal structures by topological types is a powerful tool to reveal structural correlations between the structures with different chemical composition and complexity.

the topological approach to the analysis of the MT-framework structure organization allows one to consider systematically the structures of zirconolites and their analogs and to reveal structural correlations between them.
topological analysis of crystal structure can be a powerful tool to reveal the structural similarities of complex minerals and to understand their crystal chemistry and genesis.
